title: XRepoTest: Benchmarking Multilingual Repository-Level Unit Test Generation for Large Language Models
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.25939v2 (15 September 2026; complete 20,558-word article incl. appendices, prompts, data/metric definitions and analyses read)
datasets: XRepoTest: 3,642 focal functions across five repository languages: Rust 931, Go 706, Julia 684, PHP 646, Ruby 675; 6–10 real public repositories per language, six domains.
Defects4J appears only in benchmark related-work comparison; experiment explicitly excludes Java and Python. BugsInPy and SWT-Bench are not used.
External SWE-bench Verified scores are correlated with XRepoTest metrics in one appendix; no SWE-bench bug instances are evaluated in the main test-generation benchmark.
task: Repository-level unit-test generation for real focal functions, evaluated in native Docker test/build environments. Compares five prompt contexts: standard, LSP, full file, sparse BM25 RAG, dense UniXCoder RAG. Metrics include compilation success, pass rate, macro line coverage, mutation score (Go/Rust/Ruby only), and Invocation Rate (whether generated tests directly call the focal function). Includes a small agentic headless Claude Code and one-round GPT-OSS repair study.
input_setting: Focal function from current open-source repository with optional file/LSP/retrieved context; no issue report, buggy/fixed version pair, or developer-provided expected-behavior oracle. Tests run against the actual current repository source. Mutation testing is the fault-detection proxy on three languages; IR helps identify tests that pass/exercise unrelated helpers instead of the target.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper abstract explicitly says dataset and code are public at this exact GitHub URL. Repository includes `paper.pdf`, authors' benchmark source, CI/tests, Docker evaluators and matching citation/EMNLP 2026 identity. GitHub README points to the authors' public HuggingFace dataset `solis-soict/xrepotest`.
source_commit_or_archive: GitHub default branch HEAD `39fb6ab3173136d3dac2d38ed7c98baf6c470270` (reported author commit date 2026-08-27); public MIT license; 313 tree entries, 3,349,430 bytes of source/assets/tests. Static inspection covered README, LICENSE, fetch script, dataset metadata, LLM/model wrapper, generation/evaluation/repair pipeline, Docker setup/images and language evaluators. HuggingFace dataset API confirms public, ungated `solis-soict/xrepotest`, MIT metadata, dataset commit `cd694c00d20951aef189a406abac980a6b1c49d4`, 40 JSONL files (~1.69 GB total): base 5 files ~105 MB; LSP 5 files ~106 MB; RAG 30 files ~1.48 GB. `repo_data/` raw clones are not distributed; README says they are needed only to rebuild data/images, not to evaluate with published dataset and prebuilt Docker images.
license: GitHub code MIT; HuggingFace dataset metadata/card tags MIT. Dataset consists of excerpts/metadata from upstream repositories; each repository retains its own source license. Paper CC BY 4.0. Use source-repository terms when rebuilding or redistributing original code snapshots.
weights_status: Models are a mix of hosted API and publicly available open-weight models. Paper lists exact HuggingFace/API model IDs in Appendix I, with some provider versions/date-suffixed names. Qwen models in the paper are Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-Coder-Next 80B, not the user's Qwen2.5-Coder-7B. The runner supports local vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint; user can evaluate Qwen2.5-Coder-7B as an independent new-model evaluation without modifying CATGen-like method code. No model was called.
evaluation_route: Read full article and Appendix A–K. Public GitHub package has installable Python CLI, task/data fetch script, prompt/context modes, response generation client, preprocessing, Docker-based execution, coverage/mutation evaluators, repair/agentic paths, analysis scripts and tests. README run sequence is `xrepotest run` or prompts → responses → preprocess → eval; pass a local `--api_base` and model ID. HuggingFace dataset is ungated and publicly fetchable; base setting for all five languages is ~105 MB, file context shares this data; LSP adds ~106 MB and RAG contexts ~1.48 GB. Evaluation requires Docker and published per-language images (README references `latest`, not immutable image digests). A bounded one-language Qwen run is reasonably straightforward; five-language/full-context replication entails pulling data/images, substantial generation/inference, and managing runtime. Exact full paper rerun requires 14 models and original provider/model versions; some aliases/revisions are not frozen. No code, data, Docker image or model was executed/downloaded in this audit.
blockers: The benchmark is Rust/Go/Julia/PHP/Ruby only; Java and Python were deliberately excluded. Defects4J is related work only; it is not an issue-to-BRT, buggy/fixed, or real-fault cohort. No BugsInPy/SWT-Bench experiments.

The task asks for tests of current focal code, not reproduction of a reported bug. There is no developer intended-behavior oracle or root-cause-label evaluation. IR is a direct-call heuristic and does not alone guarantee semantic validation; the paper itself shows Julia dispatch cases where direct name invocation can still miss the intended overload.

Full paper rerun requires all 14 heterogeneous models; hosted providers and some model IDs/revisions may change. User Qwen2.5-Coder-7B differs from paper's Qwen3 models, so that is an independent evaluation, not exact replication.

Requires Docker and five language-native images/toolchains; README uses mutable `latest` image references. Raw `repo_data/` source clones are not bundled, though they are unnecessary when published data and prebuilt images remain accessible.
Mutation score is implemented only for Go, Rust and Ruby. Julia/PHP mutation tooling is not available/compatible.
concept_fit: Strong supplementary test-evaluation benchmark: repository-realistic execution, context ablations and the Invocation Rate expose passing/coverage results that do not actually target the assigned focal function. Failure taxonomy finds API hallucination, type/memory and incorrect logic/assertions. However, this is not a concept-guided test method or root-cause study; it has no bug-report, fixed-version, F2P oracle, or developer ground truth. It can test whether the user's model generates executable, target-invoking, mutation-killing tests in five additional languages.
recommendation: Promote as a strong/easy own-model evaluation route if the user wants repository-level test-quality metrics beyond Java/Python. The MIT source + public MIT-tagged HF dataset + Docker evaluators and OpenAI-compatible local vLLM route make a bounded Qwen2.5-Coder-7B evaluation feasible without reimplementing the paper; start with one language and `standard` or `file_context`, not all 1.69 GB context variants. Do not choose it as the primary Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT-Bench or issue-reproduction dataset: it evaluates current source in five non-Java/Python languages. For direct Java buggy/fixed detection and metric validity, #74 remains the top fit; #65 offers strong complementary repository-level evaluation and a novel invocation metric. No run performed.

Paper Section 5 and Appendices E–J: 14 models, context comparisons, mutation outcomes, failure taxonomy, agentic/repair ablations and model IDs.
Paper explicitly says Java/Python excluded due prior work; Defects4J appears as a related-work benchmark only.
Paper Data Availability/abstract and README identify official repository and HuggingFace data.

README gives public HuggingFace fetch command, data grouping/size pathway, Docker prerequisites and local endpoint CLI. `repo_data/` is omitted but not needed for evaluation against prebuilt images.
HuggingFace API confirms dataset public and ungated, MIT metadata, 40 JSONL files over base/LSP/RAG; sizes computed from public file tree.
